Where each statement of fact on the Tiny Tapeout FPGA wiring pages comes from. A statement nobody has checked says so. A board is named by where it was seen on the day of the measurement, because that is all the record gives.

- Which demo board header is cabled to which Pmod HAT port (INPUT to JA, BIDIR to JB and OUTPUT to JC), and the 18 wires that have a Raspberry Pi GPIO to themselves (every wire except `ui_in[1]`, `ui_in[2]`, `ui_in[3]`, `uio[1]`, `uio[2]` and `uio[3]`): measured: read with the pin identification design (each FPGA pin sends its own pin number, and the Raspberry Pi reads which number arrives on which GPIO) on 29 September 2026, and again by the boot check (`fpgas-verify`) on 4 October 2026, on the three Tiny Tapeout FPGA boards seen at welland's sw2 p33, p35 and p36 on those days; the host at sw2 p34 was not powered either time. On 3 September 2026 those three ports had the demo boards whose microcontrollers have the USB serial numbers `4df39a7a6856f86f`, `8c46329b33590ecb` and `a2961e5cac65b25f` ([`docs/hardware/site-welland.md`](https://github.com/fpgas-online/fpgas.online-test-designs/blob/main/docs/hardware/site-welland.md)); whether the same boards were there on the days of the measurement is not recorded. The record is the hand-written [`docs/hardware/tt-fpga-pin-mapping.md`](https://github.com/fpgas-online/fpgas.online-test-designs/blob/main/docs/hardware/tt-fpga-pin-mapping.md) that this generator replaced, as it stood at commit `ef38e22`; and, wire by wire, the scan decoded on those boards, kept as the expected values of `test_a_tt_cabled_as_the_fleet_passes_and_ja_jc_swapped_fails` in [`designs/pmod-pin-id/host/test_identify_pmod_pins.py`](https://github.com/fpgas-online/fpgas.online-test-designs/blob/main/designs/pmod-pin-id/host/test_identify_pmod_pins.py) (as commit `8987ede` left it), whose comment gives the same ports and days. The measurement joins an iCE40 pin to a Raspberry Pi GPIO; the header pin and the port pin in between are from the entries below.
- The wires no measurement covers (`ui_in[1]`, `ui_in[2]`, `ui_in[3]`, `uio[1]`, `uio[2]` and `uio[3]`): from the design: it follows the pattern of the measured wires (bit n of a group on the pin of that place in its header and port); not measured by us. Since issue 142 of fpgas.online-test-designs (two wires that end on one Raspberry Pi GPIO could not be told apart) the pin identification design sends on such wires in turns so that each can be read, but no result of that is recorded in this repository.
- The demo board's three Pmod connectors are printed INPUT (`ui_in`), BIDIR (`uio`) and OUTPUT (`uo_out`): Tiny Tapeout's published demo board design (github.com/TinyTapeout/tt-demo-pcb: README, doc/img/pmods-io.png, doc/img/tt-etr-dbv3p2-pinout.png, doc/img/tt-etr-dbv3-board.jpg), read 6 October 2026; not verified by us on a board.
- They are on the bottom edge, in that order from left to right, with the board held so that its "Tiny Tapeout Demoboard" text reads upright: Tiny Tapeout's published demo board design (github.com/TinyTapeout/tt-demo-pcb: README, doc/img/pmods-io.png, doc/img/tt-etr-dbv3p2-pinout.png, doc/img/tt-etr-dbv3-board.jpg), read 6 October 2026; not verified by us on a board.
- Each is a female right-angle 2x6 socket, numbered as Digilent numbers a host port: Tiny Tapeout's published demo board design (github.com/TinyTapeout/tt-demo-pcb: README, doc/img/pmods-io.png, doc/img/tt-etr-dbv3p2-pinout.png, doc/img/tt-etr-dbv3-board.jpg), read 6 October 2026: the schematic says "PMOD host (female) headers, using digilent's numbering", and the pinout poster says "the connectors on this board are female and designed to operate as the host"; not verified by us on a board.
- The board's own 3.3 V supply is on pins 6 and 12 of each: Tiny Tapeout's published demo board design (github.com/TinyTapeout/tt-demo-pcb: README, doc/img/pmods-io.png, doc/img/tt-etr-dbv3p2-pinout.png, doc/img/tt-etr-dbv3-board.jpg), read 6 October 2026 (the schematic puts +3V3 on pins 6 and 12); not verified by us on a board.
- In the maker's drawing of the board, pin 1 is the square pad under the label i0, b0 or o0, at the right-hand end of the row farther from the board edge. No "1" is printed there: Tiny Tapeout's published demo board design (github.com/TinyTapeout/tt-demo-pcb: README, doc/img/pmods-io.png, doc/img/tt-etr-dbv3p2-pinout.png, doc/img/tt-etr-dbv3-board.jpg), read 6 October 2026 (the render of the board); not checked by us on a board.
- JA, JB and JC are 2x6 Pmod host ports (female sockets): Digilent's Pmod HAT Adapter Reference Manual, read from a copy on 6 October 2026: "2x6 Pmod host ports"; not verified by us on a board.
- Pins 6 and 12 of each port are tied to the HAT's 3.3 V supply, and pins 5 and 11 are ground: Digilent's Pmod HAT Adapter Reference Manual, read from a copy on 6 October 2026: "Pins #6 and #12 of each Pmod port are tied to the HAT Adapter's 3V3 rail"; not verified by us on a board.
- Digilent's product photograph of the HAT shows a printed "1" beside one end of each port's inner row, and "3V3" and "GND" at the other end. This is legible for JA and JB; JC's label is not legible in the photograph: Digilent's Pmod HAT Adapter Reference Manual, read from a copy on 6 October 2026 (its product photograph); not checked by us on a board.
- On our boards each cable is a female-to-female 10-pin ribbon cable (0.1 inch pitch), joined to the female socket at each end through a strip of pin header, with the 3.3 V pin left out: pins 6 and 12 are not carried, so the two boards' 3.3 V supplies are not joined: Tim Ansell, 7 October 2026, answering our question of 6 October; he believes the ribbon cables are whiteeeen 10-pin flat ribbon cables, 0.1 inch pitch, female to female sockets, about 7.87 inch (200 mm), IDC connectors (Amazon product B094RGMBS9). How the 10-pin cable sits on the 12-pin socket (which row ends are left free) is not recorded by us.
- Both ends are female sockets, so each cable needs a male end at each board: it follows from the two makers' statements that the sockets are female; not checked by us on a board.
- If a straight twelve-wire cable is used instead, it joins the two boards' 3.3 V supplies: it follows from the two makers' statements that pins 6 and 12 are each board's 3.3 V supply. That the cables are straight through is from [`docs/hardware/rpi-hat-pmod.md`](https://github.com/fpgas-online/fpgas.online-test-designs/blob/main/docs/hardware/rpi-hat-pmod.md), and the measured wires are where a straight-through cable puts them.
- Seen on the cameras of the boards shown as fpga-1 and fpga-3 on tinytapeout.fpgas.online on 6 October 2026: a black two-row housing is plugged on each of the demo board's three connectors, and a rainbow ribbon runs from them on fpga-1. Neither the wires nor any pin 1 mark can be made out: two camera stills taken on 6 October 2026; nobody has looked at the boards themselves for this.
- Digilent's specification says: "the pin numbering conventions for the 2x6 connectors are non-standard and are mirrored between the host connector and the peripheral board connector": Digilent's Pmod Interface Specification, revised 28 October 2020, read from a copy on 6 October 2026.
- Which iCE40 pin is which Tiny Tapeout signal (`ui_in`, `uo_out`, `uio`, the clock, the reset, the LED): [`designs/_shared/tt_fpga_platform.py`](https://github.com/fpgas-online/fpgas.online-test-designs/blob/main/designs/_shared/tt_fpga_platform.py), which follows the `fabricfoxv2` pin file of Tiny Tapeout's tt-support-tools. From the design; a test keeps these tables equal to that file. Measured by us only as far as the entries above say.
- That bit 0 to bit 7 of a group are on pins 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 9, 10 of its demo board header, that pins 1 to 6 are one row and pins 7 to 12 the other, and that pins 5 and 11 are ground and pins 6 and 12 are 3.3 V: Tiny Tapeout's pinout documents and Digilent's Pmod specification, as [`docs/hardware/pmod-tt.md`](https://github.com/fpgas-online/fpgas.online-test-designs/blob/main/docs/hardware/pmod-tt.md) and [`docs/hardware/pmod.md`](https://github.com/fpgas-online/fpgas.online-test-designs/blob/main/docs/hardware/pmod.md) summarise them; not verified by us against a board.
- Which Raspberry Pi GPIO each Pmod HAT pin is, and that some pins of two ports are the same GPIO: the DesignSpark Pmod HAT driver and Digilent's schematic of the HAT, as [`docs/hardware/rpi-hat-pmod.md`](https://github.com/fpgas-online/fpgas.online-test-designs/blob/main/docs/hardware/rpi-hat-pmod.md) cites them; a test keeps these tables equal to the list in [`designs/pmod-pin-id/host/identify_pmod_pins.py`](https://github.com/fpgas-online/fpgas.online-test-designs/blob/main/designs/pmod-pin-id/host/identify_pmod_pins.py). Not verified by us with a meter; the measured wires agree with it.
- The serial port (which two signals, which two RP2350 GPIOs, the speed): [`designs/_shared/tt_fpga_platform.py`](https://github.com/fpgas-online/fpgas.online-test-designs/blob/main/designs/_shared/tt_fpga_platform.py) and [`designs/_host/tt_test_wrapper.py`](https://github.com/fpgas-online/fpgas.online-test-designs/blob/main/designs/_host/tt_test_wrapper.py); a test keeps these tables equal to both. The `uart` test goes through the microcontroller and not through the Pmod HAT. It passed on 2 October 2026 on the three Tiny Tapeout FPGA boards seen at welland's sw2 p33, p35 and p36 that day (the results in [`docs/verify.md`](https://github.com/fpgas-online/fpgas.online-test-designs/blob/main/docs/verify.md)). Nobody has used these two signals as a serial port from the Raspberry Pi's GPIO.
- The iCE40's configuration pins, and that the breakout has no SPI flash: [`docs/hardware/tt-fpga.md`](https://github.com/fpgas-online/fpgas.online-test-designs/blob/main/docs/hardware/tt-fpga.md), from the breakout's published design (TinyTapeout/breakout-pcb), checked there on 4 October 2026; not measured by us.
- The RP2350 GPIOs that load the FPGA and make its clock: [`designs/_host/tt_fpga_program.py`](https://github.com/fpgas-online/fpgas.online-test-designs/blob/main/designs/_host/tt_fpga_program.py), the loader, and [`designs/_host/tt_test_wrapper.py`](https://github.com/fpgas-online/fpgas.online-test-designs/blob/main/designs/_host/tt_test_wrapper.py), the serial bridge, which starts the clock again. A test holds the four loading pins (in both of the loader's ways of sending), the clock pin and the clock's frequency to those two files, and the frequency to the platform file.
- The other RP2350 GPIO numbers (those on the 24 signals, and the one on the reset): Tiny Tapeout's pinout documents for the version 3 demo board, as [`docs/hardware/pmod-tt.md`](https://github.com/fpgas-online/fpgas.online-test-designs/blob/main/docs/hardware/pmod-tt.md) summarises them. Our loader, run with `--gpio-release`, starts the clock and then sets the GPIOs of the 24 signals to inputs; without that flag it starts no clock and leaves GPIO17 to GPIO40 as they were. Our serial bridge starts the clock itself and uses two of the signals; the rest, and the reset's, are not verified by us.
- Which segment of the display each bit of `uo_out` lights, and that a to f are the outer ring in that order: Tiny Tapeout's board specification, as [`docs/hardware/tt-fpga.md`](https://github.com/fpgas-online/fpgas.online-test-designs/blob/main/docs/hardware/tt-fpga.md) gives it, and [`designs/tt-display`](https://github.com/fpgas-online/fpgas.online-test-designs/blob/main/designs/tt-display), which is written to it and describes its pattern as one segment running round the outer ring, a to f (a test holds the place of g and of the dot to that design). Where a is, and which way round the ring runs, is not recorded; none of it is verified by us segment by segment.
- That the three-colour LED lights when its pin is low: a comment in [`designs/_shared/tt_fpga_platform.py`](https://github.com/fpgas-online/fpgas.online-test-designs/blob/main/designs/_shared/tt_fpga_platform.py); not verified by us.
- That the demo board's DIP switches are on the `ui_in` signals: [`docs/hardware/tt-fpga.md`](https://github.com/fpgas-online/fpgas.online-test-designs/blob/main/docs/hardware/tt-fpga.md), which gives no source for it; not verified by us. How the switches must be set while the Raspberry Pi drives `ui_in` is not recorded.
